packageRules.description: The shared conventions are pinned in TWO files — the catalogue and the settings plugin — and a repository holding one at a version the other does not is exactly the split that breaks quietly: the plugins load, the build configures, and one half of the contract is a release behind. Grouping them is what keeps the pair moving as a pair.
Kotlin and its plugins are built against a specific compiler version; a mismatched pair fails the build rather than reporting a version problem.
Exposed core and jdbc go in as a single version.
kotlinx libraries move independently of each other but are noisy one PR at a time.

Testcontainers and the Postgres driver are used by nothing but the tests, and verifying either means the same thing: bring up a container and run the suite against it. One PR is one such run instead of two.

Major updates get their own PR: they cannot be merged without looking. The move from sborka 0.1.x to 0.2.x brought two new lint rules that found six real holes — worth reading, not worth merging blind.
